lines.l: Oh, one of those alone four nine-foot sacks standing at the old turn road
Down in Mississippi, down in Mississippi, down in Mississippi
The season was always open on me
Down in Mississippi where I was born
Down in Mississippi, where I come from
I remember, I used to walk down that gravel road
Walking with my grandma, Mississippi son
I went to get some water
And that fountain had a sign
I was so glad I had my grandma and my papa
No, I won't leave you out, grandpa
My grandpa was so proud of me, y'all
I went down in Forest, Mississippi one time there
But I integrated a wash of tears
My grandbaby, Mavis, she went up in that washeteria and washed her clothes. And all the black ladies followed her own up in there.
I'm proud of my grandbaby. I saw many more of those times as I lived in Mississippi.
I'm so glad I can say that I saw every one of those signs. Dr. King saw that every one of those signs were taken down.
